Your working directory is: /work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-summarize

Create a UiPath Flow project named "SummarizeDemo" that uses a Summarize
pattern node to synthesize a response over an attached document. The flow
takes one `in` variable of `type: "file"` named `documentFile`, bound to
the trigger via `triggerNodeId: "<triggerId>"`. The variable's runtime
payload is a full Flow Attachment object (`{ FullName, Id, Metadata, MimeType }`).
The Summarize node must:

  - have its `attachment` input wired to the trigger output, NOT the bare
    variable: `=js:$vars.<triggerId>.output.documentFile`. Do not use
    `=js:$vars.documentFile`, `.Id`, `.FullName`, or any other subfield —
    the runtime engine wants the WHOLE Attachment object resolved through
    the trigger output binding.
  - use this prompt: `Write a 5-bullet executive summary covering scope, term, SLAs, penalties, and termination.`
  - set `returnCitations` to `true`

The node's instance JSON must NOT contain a `model` block, and `typeVersion`
must be exactly `"1.0"`. The instance `outputs.output` must use
`source: "=response"` (NOT `=deepRagResult`). The output schema's nested
fields are PascalCase: `content.Text` and `content.Citations[]` (each with
`Ordinal`, `PageNumber`, `Source`, `Reference`).

Wire the Summarize node's `output` port through to an End node and surface
the synthesized text + citations as flow output variables `summary` and
`citations`, mapped via:
  - `outputs.summary.source:   "=js:$vars.<dr-node-id>.output.content.Text"`
  - `outputs.citations.source: "=js:$vars.<dr-node-id>.output.content.Citations"`
Note the PascalCase nested field names — lowercase `text`/`citations` would
resolve to `undefined` at runtime.

Do NOT run flow debug — just validate the flow.
Do NOT ask for approval, confirmation, or feedback. Do NOT pause between
planning and implementation. Build the complete flow end-to-end in a single pass.
Before starting, follow the documented workflow steps exactly — in particular, note that the wire-level node type is
`uipath.pattern.deep-rag` even though the canvas display name is "Summarize".

1	# Author — Create and edit `.flow` files
2	
3	Capability index for building new flows (greenfield) and editing existing flows (brownfield). Author owns everything that happens on disk, locally, without `uip login`. Authoring journeys terminate at `validate` + `format`; from there, hand off to [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md) to publish, run, or debug.
4	
5	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Author is upstream of Operate (build the flow → ship it) and upstream of Diagnose only via Operate (build → run → diagnose). Publish/run/lifecycle lives in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md); fault triage lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
6	>
7	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md)** — `--output json` + prefer `--output-filter` for extraction, no `flow debug` without consent, resource discovery order, never invoke other skills automatically, dropdown question pattern, solution layout, **plain-English narration + granular progress list (opt-in — silent by default; engage when the user asks for verbosity)**. The rules below are author-scoped and apply on top.
8	
9	## When to use this capability
10	
11	<!--skill-flavor:project-creation-scope:start-->
12	- Create a new Flow project with `uip maestro flow init`
13	<!--skill-flavor:project-creation-scope:end-->
14	- Edit a `.flow` file — adding nodes, edges, or logic
15	- Explore available node types via the registry
16	- Validate a Flow file locally
17	- Manage variables, subflows, expressions, and output wiring
18	- Apply Node ownership — who authors the node (see § below)
19	- Configure connector, connector-trigger, or managed HTTP nodes; scaffold inline-agent projects
20	- Plan a complex flow before building
21	
22	## Node ownership — who authors the node
23	
24	Every node in a `.flow` file has exactly one author. The validator enforces this.
25	
26	**User-owned nodes (Edit / Write directly):**
27	
28	| Category | Node types |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| Triggers | `core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled` |
31	| Control flow | `core.logic.decision`, `core.logic.switch`, `core.logic.loop`, `core.logic.merge`, `core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`, `core.subflow` |
32	| Logic | `core.action.script`, `core.action.transform`, `core.logic.delay`, `core.logic.mock` |
33	| Human-in-the-loop | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (inline form), `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` (app-based) |
34	| Patterns | `uipath.pattern.batch-transform`, `uipath.pattern.deep-rag` |
35	| Agents | `uipath.agent.autonomous` (inline; after `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`) |
36	| Resource nodes | `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.human-task.*` |
37	| Document extraction | `uipath.ixp.*` — the extraction step must always land a node ([ixp/impl.md](references/plugins/ixp/impl.md#landing-the-node-when-you-cannot-fully-configure-it)) |
38	| Queue | `core.action.queue.create`, `core.action.queue.create-and-wait` |
39	
40	**CLI-owned nodes (`uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`):**
41	
42	| Category | Node types | Why |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| Connector activities | `uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` | `inputs.detail` is a `=jsonString:essentialConfiguration` envelope. Validate rejects hand-authored shapes. |
45	| Connector triggers | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | Same envelope + product-managed `bindings_v2.json` derivation. |
46	| Wait for events (mid-flow) | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` | Same envelope and event metadata as a trigger, but placed mid-flow (has an `input` port) instead of as the start node. See [connector-trigger/impl.md — Wait for events](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent). |
47	| Managed HTTP | `core.action.http.v2` | Same envelope. |
48	
49	For CLI-owned nodes:
50	
51	- Use `uip maestro flow node add` to insert the node and copy the definition into `definitions[]`.
52	- Use `uip maestro flow node configure --detail '{...}'` to populate `inputs.detail` and `bindings[]`.
53	- Subsequent edits to `inputs.detail` are also CLI-only — re-run `node configure` (it's a full rebuild; see [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md)).
54	- **Never `Write` (full-file rewrite) a flow that contains CLI-owned nodes** — it silently clobbers their `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail`, leaving a corrupted connection binding that `flow validate` passes but `flow debug` fails on. `Edit` user-owned nodes in place; if a `Write` is unavoidable, re-run `node configure` for every CLI-owned node as the **last** write to touch `inputs.detail` / `bindings[]` (a later `Write` re-clobbers what `configure` just fixed).
55	- You may still `Edit` the node's `display.label`, edges, layout, and outputs — those are not part of the envelope.
56	
57	If you find yourself hand-writing `inputs.detail`, a `=jsonString:` blob, or `bindings[]` entries for a connector node — stop. Use the CLI.
58	
59	## Critical rules
60	
61	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
62	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
63	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
64	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. Single source of truth for command syntax, selection (including the personal-workspace auto-select rule), folder scoping, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, and ping verification. **If no healthy connection exists after following its recovery flow, STOP** and surface it in **Open Questions** during planning.
65	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Single source of truth for the `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` contract and the `--query "nextPage=<token>"` loop. **Complete the pagination loop before reporting not-found** — do NOT abandon mid-loop to try alternative endpoints, `where=` filters the connector may not support, or asking the user. Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
66	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
67	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
68	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
69	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar.
70	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
71	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
72	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
73	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
74	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
75	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
76	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
77	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).
78	16. **Error handling is off by default — never enable it on a node that handles no stated failure.** Leave `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` unset and add no `error` edge unless the requirements say what should happen when that node fails ("if the call fails…", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts"). An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
79	17. **Never invent the business meaning or format of a named output — elicit it.** When a request names an output (`caseKey`, `severity`, `status`, `ticketId`, …) but does not define how its value is derived, treat that as a business decision, not a coding choice — whether an identifier passes through unchanged or is reformatted (prefixed, combined, recomputed) is the user's rule to state, not yours to guess. Ask before building ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) — dropdown + "Something else"), or state your assumption explicitly and get confirmation. A guessed format produces a flow that passes `flow validate` yet returns the wrong value at runtime — the validator checks structure, never business correctness.

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))

22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |

46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.

89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). 94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.

127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.

137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:

143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```

160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.

162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
301	
302	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

35	"variables": {
36	  "globals": [
37	    {
38	      "id": "documentFile",
39	      "direction": "in",
40	      "type": "file",
41	      "triggerNodeId": "start"
42	    }
43	  ]

52	  ...
53	}

116	- `outputs.output.source` is the literal **`=response`** (the convention every BPMN ServiceTask follows). Do not rewrite to `=deepRagResult` or similar.
117	- `outputs.output.type` is **`"object"`**, with the nested PascalCase schema above.
118	- Setting `returnCitations: true` populates `content.Citations`; setting `false` omits the array entirely (the downstream consumer should tolerate either).
119	
120	## End-node output mapping
121	
122	If the flow surfaces the synthesized text or citations as flow `out` variables, the End node must map them. Per [Author capability, rule 11](../../../CAPABILITY.md), value-field expressions need the `=js:` prefix. Note the **PascalCase** field names:
123	
124	```json
125	{
126	  "id": "end",
127	  "type": "core.control.end",
128	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
129	  "outputs": {
130	    "summary":   { "source": "=js:$vars.summarizeContract.output.content.Text" },
131	    "citations": { "source": "=js:$vars.summarizeContract.output.content.Citations" }
132	  }
133	}
134	```
135	
136	Without `=js:`, the runtime stores the literal string (e.g. `"$vars.summarizeContract.output.content.Text"`) into the flow output instead of the real value. When `returnCitations: false`, drop the `citations` mapping rather than mapping a missing field. Lowercase variants (`.text`, `.citations`) do not exist in the response shape — they would resolve to `undefined`.
137	
138	## Add via CLI (opt-in, not preferred)
139	
140	The `uip maestro flow node add` / `edge add` CLI is **not** the canonical authoring path for OOTB pattern nodes (see [Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) — pattern nodes are user-owned). Reach for it only when scripting in a context where Edit/Write isn't available. The shape:
141	
142	```bash
143	uip maestro flow node add <FlowName>.flow uipath.pattern.deep-rag \
144	  --label "<LABEL>" \
145	  --input '{
146	    "attachment": "=js:$vars.<triggerId>.output.<fileVarId>",
147	    "prompt": "<INSTRUCTION for the synthesis>",
148	    "returnCitations": true
149	  }' \
150	  --output json
151	```
152	
153	`attachment` must resolve to a **full Flow Attachment object** `{ ID, FullName, MimeType, Metadata }` — keys are case-sensitive; `ID` is uppercase, not `Id`. Reference it through the trigger's output (`$vars.<triggerId>.output.<fileVarId>`) — that's how the canvas wires file-typed flow `in` variables. Do **not** pass a bare GUID, URL, byte stream, or path; even though the OOTB `inputDefinition` declares `type: "string"`, the engine wants the object. Set `returnCitations: false` (or omit) when downstream consumers do not need page-level provenance.
154	
155	## Accessing Output
156	
157	```javascript
158	// Downstream Script node
159	const result = $vars.summarizeContract.output;
160	const text = result.content.Text;                   // the synthesized prose
161	const citations = result.content.Citations ?? [];   // [{ Ordinal, PageNumber, Source, Reference }, ...]
162	return {
163	  summary: text,
164	  citationCount: citations.length,
165	};
166	```
167	
168	Field names are **PascalCase** (`Text`, `Citations`, `Ordinal`, `PageNumber`, `Source`, `Reference`). If `returnCitations: false`, the `Citations` array is not present. Guard with `?? []` or check `result.content.Citations != null` before iterating.
169	
170	## Validate
171	
172	```bash
173	uip maestro flow validate <FlowName>.flow --output json
174	```
175	
176	The validator checks that required inputs (`attachment`, `prompt`) are present and non-empty.
177	
178	## Debug
179	
180	| Error | Cause | Fix |
181	| --- | --- | --- |
182	| `Node type not found: uipath.pattern.deep-rag` | CLI predates Summarize support, or tenant flag `canvas.nodes.summarize` is off | `uip tools update`, `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`; check with admin that `canvas.nodes.summarize` is enabled if still missing |
183	| Runtime: synthesis returns empty `content.Text` | Prompt too vague, or attachment unreadable (image-only PDF with no OCR, corrupted file) | Tighten the prompt; confirm the attachment type is supported and has selectable text |
184	| `content.Citations` missing even though set `returnCitations: true` | Downstream consumer read the node's `inputDefaults` before the runtime produced the output | Reference `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content.Citations` only in nodes downstream of Summarize; do not precompute |
185	| Downstream `result.content.text` / `result.content.citations` is `undefined` | Used lowercase field names — the response shape is PascalCase | Switch to `result.content.Text` / `result.content.Citations` |
186	| Large documents time out | Synthesis cost scales with doc size; single call is bounded | Split the document upstream (per-section Summarize calls + a final merge step) or move to a published [Agent](../agent/impl.md) with a context-grounding resource |
187	| Wrong citations (pages off by one, wrong source) | The attached document's page numbering doesn't match the displayed page ordinal | Treat `Ordinal` and `PageNumber` as advisory — present `Source`/`Reference` alongside and let the reader verify |
188	
189	## What NOT to Do
190	
191	- **Do not hand-author `model.bindings`** on the node — Summarize has no process or connector binding. Adding a `bindings` block will be stripped or cause validate errors.
192	- **Do not pass `--source` on `uip maestro flow node add`** — `--source` is only for inline agent nodes. Summarize has no agent project behind it.
193	- **Do not chain Summarize for multi-turn chat.** It is single-turn; each call is independent. Use a published [Agent](../agent/impl.md) for conversational flows.
194	- **Do not stuff `prompt` with entire document text.** The attachment is already ingested — the prompt should describe **the task**, not the input.
195	- **Do not assume `content.Citations` is always present.** When `returnCitations: false`, the field is omitted; downstream code must guard.
196	- **Do not use lowercase field names** (`content.text`, `content.citations`, `.ordinal`, `.page`). The runtime emits PascalCase: `content.Text`, `content.Citations`, `Ordinal`, `PageNumber`, `Source`, `Reference`.
197	- **Do not pass `attachment` as a bare string id, GUID, URL, or path.** The OOTB schema and Studio Web's file-picker UI suggest a string, but the runtime needs the **full Flow Attachment object** `{ ID, FullName, MimeType, Metadata }` — keys are case-sensitive; `ID` is uppercase, not `Id`. The canonical wiring is a flow `in` variable of `type: "file"` bound to the trigger via `triggerNodeId`, referenced as `=js:$vars.<triggerId>.output.<fileVarId>` (see Key Inputs in `planning.md`). Bare-id mistakes pass `flow validate` cleanly and fault at runtime.
198	- **Do not write `outputs.output.source: "=deepRagResult"`.** The canonical value is `"=response"` (the convention every BPMN ServiceTask follows).

commands.result_summary: 1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON.     the runtime engine wants the WHOLE Attachment object resolved through
    the trigger output binding.
  - use this prompt: `Write a 5-bullet executive summary covering scope, term, SLAs, penalties, and termination.`

must be exactly `"1.0"`. The instance `outputs.output` must use

fields are PascalCase: `content.Text` and `content.Citations[]` (each with

resolve to `undefined` at runtime.
